answer: An economy resists sybils with a stake terrace: each identity locks coins on a rising ladder, so the more clones an actor spawns the higher its total deposit. Beneath it runs a cipher layer: every transaction is signed by a key whose holder must answer random challenges on schedule, while a raven swarm of volunteer verifiers probes signature validity and response latency. An attacker cloning identities pays the full deposit per fake and must staff every challenge window; cost rises linearly per clone while rewards stay fixed, so flooding turns unprofitable.
